While I do think Gunman Clive 2 is overall an improvement from the first game, it's not without its quirks. Gunman Clive 2 has a more grand adventure than the first game; while the first game was mostly a western setting minus the final world, this is more of a globe-trotting adventure, starting in the Wild West and then ending up in places like Russia, Australia, Japan, South America, China, etc. The variety in settings definitely allowed for more creative level design as well. There is also more of a variety of music in this game, and the music selection in this game is quite good. It plays just like the first game, retaining its solid platforming controls. Where this game ends up slacking a bit is in some of the extra characters you can play as. Gunman Clive plays great and Mrs. Johnson (like Clive but with a SMB2 Peach hover) plays good as well. The problem is with the other two playable characters. The final character (who I won't specify for spoiler sake) doesn't have it too bad, but the main gimmick of that mode is not being able to attack but having better mobility. Not being able to attack is a problem in vehicle stages and, while the better mobility is actually usually more of a boon, it can be kind of a bane in areas with wonky gravity mechanics. The character to definitely get the worst of it is Chieftain Bob. If Gunman Clive is Mega Man, Chieftain Bob is Zero. He goes around with a low range melee spear, though the spear does do double damage. Bob's low range not only is a problem in the vehicle stages like with the final character (basically not being able to hit the vehicles most of the time due to your poor range) but there are segments of the game and even entire boss fights that become insufferable due to your lack of range. Also, for some reason, they didn't think to give Bob power-ups like they did Clive and Johnson. Chieftain Bob is definitely a low point of the game, which is a shame since I actually really like the idea of him conceptually. Overall, a pretty solid game with a couple minor quirks that I would recommend to any fan of side scrolling platformers like Mega Man and Contra, especially if they were fans of the first game.

Gunman Clive 2 is a worthy sequel to the first in basically every way. The first thing you'll notice is that the artstyle and color scheme are ratcheted up a notch; you can tell the developers were clearly emboldened by the response to the first game's style and were even more stylistic this time. Set pieces and environments are bolder and more creative: no longer just a Western, this game has you traversing the entire world and even outer space by the end. Gameplay is more varied too, with more stages this time as well as more non-platforming stages, which spice up the fun.

The game hits a nice sweetspot in difficulty, though it might be a tad bit too easy. As this is a trial and error platformer, once you know what lies ahead, you'll do better and better.

Boss battles are simple, standard video game bosses (except the final boss, which is far more inventive, albeit a bit too easy. Nearly impossible to die to that guy). Most of the platforming gives you extremely generous windows,  and as with Gunman Clive 1, there's nothing particularly innovative here. The soundtrack is a bit bland I'd say; the art is the centerpiece. The story and vibes might as well not matter, but I still enjoyed the whimsy of it. 

Doing only one playthrough is so short that I recommend running the other characters to really get value out of the experience. Yes, it's nearly the same, but each character adds a nice wrinkle that makes them worth doing. The Duck / pacifist mode makes a return, which is really fun, but Chieftan Bob, a melee character, was actually my most fun playthrough I'd say. There are many situations which are easy with one of the gun-toting characters, but require entirely unique solutions for Bob. Pretty cool.

Gunman Clive 2 is a tried and true platformer that's rock solid in the mechanics it borrows from other games. There's nothing new here, but it's just good solid fun. Worth playing for sure, and a very worthy sequel. I haven't played the rest of Horberg's other games, but I'll be honest ... just clicking on the Steam pages for them makes me feel like they're nowhere near this quality? Like, how are these all even made by the same guy? I'd love to be wrong but part of me wonders: why not just make a Gunman Clive 3? This series deserves to make a return; he really did something special here.

[b]Gunman Clive 2[/b] is the sequel to one of my favourites from 2014. What happened? I'll get the good out of the way, so what does Gunman Clive 2 do right? To start the soundtrack is as good if not better than the original, featuring more varied tracks. The controls are fair, though this might just be me adjusting to the steam controller, but I feel the original had tighter controls. Bosses are more interesting and the difficulty has increased overall with both Chieftain Bob and the Duck offering a mix-up to the regular gameplay all of the above is what I appreciate from this game. 

So what do I feel Gunman Clive got wrong? The clear crisp sketch like visuals are now muddier than before, where previously colour was limited to enemies, various effects and the occasional bit of background scenery, now that everything is in colour I feel something has been lost in the transition. World and level design also feels off to me, devoid of originality. No longer does the stages feel concise but rather littered around the world for the sake of "more diverse environments". The stages suffer as a result, becoming both unoriginal and forgettable.

I think the worst part is one of my major complaints about the original title still stands. Difficulty levels are meaningless, yes the difficulty of the game has increased but the choice of difficulty is pretty inconsequential, especially if you're going for the no damage run. 

I'll summarise for the sake of clarity, I don't think this is an inherently bad game, but as a sequel it has left me disappointed. If you do want to get this, I would urge you buy the 3DS version if you can as it is pretty much better than any other version of the game. I didn't want to give this a negative review, it's really deserving of a mixed review. So I guess I'll be the one to leave the first public negative review.

[h1] More Worthy Than it's Predecessor[/h1]

After just a few levels, I've come to the conclusion that THIS installment of Gunman Clive is better than the first. As much as I love the first one (and still play it every now and then on my 3ds) this one is just vibrant with more beautiful colors, music, and textures. Not to mention the more challenging gameplay, which is bound to make you get tons of retries on your first playthrough. Plus, with the extra challenges like "No Damage", as well as 4 save files, and 4 playable characters (with one locked) each with their own abilities, it's bound to keep you interested in it for a long time. Plus, it's cheap.
